sub: The numbers that decide when a farmer is warned, how the region map is coloured, and when a farm turns to Watch or Alarm. Every change keeps the old value, who changed it and why.
what_text: A rule is one number that turns data into a decision. For example, "Frost night" is 0 °C: when the forecast for a night is 0 °C or colder, farmers near it are warned about frost. Rules are used in three places:
where_weather_text: Writes each farmer's weekly plan and the weather warnings in the app (frost, heat, heavy rain, sowing rain, dust).
where_dryness_text: Colours every district on the region map in the admin and on the public View page (Normal, Dry, Very dry).
where_field_text: Reads each farm from satellite pictures and gives it a status: Normal, Watch or Alarm.
today: Today these numbers are still fixed in the code (farm_doctor/weather_planner.py and planFromWeather in the app). Once the backend exists, the jobs and the app read them from here, so a change here reaches farmers without a new app version.
advice: Change a little at a time and only for a reason you can name. Example: farmers in Makhmur stop reading heat warnings at 31 °C because it is hot every day, so try 33 °C and watch for two weeks.
no_history: This rule has its starting value. No changes yet.
why_ph: For example: farmers in Makhmur ignore heat warnings at 31 °C
why_needed: Write a reason, so others know why it changed.
out_of_range: The value is outside the allowed range.
